There are two possible situations that can describe acts of invisible support.  The first possibility entails a situation where "recipients are completely unaware of the supportive transaction between themselves and support-givers".  For example, a spouse may choose to spontaneously take care of housework without mentioning it to the other couple-member.  Invisible support also occurs when "recipients are aware of an act that takes place but do not interpret the act as a supportive exchange".
